prompt: With the default `json-file` driver and no options, how large may a container's log grow?
hint: What did `du` say after three seconds?

choices.text: Without limit, until the disk is full
choices.why: Right: rotation has to be asked for.

choices.text: Up to 100 MB, then it rotates
choices.why: There is no default size; it grew to 183 MB in three seconds.

choices.text: Up to whatever memory limit the container was given
choices.why: The log is a file on the host's disk, not memory.

choices.text: Nothing is kept until `docker logs` asks
choices.why: The daemon writes every line as it arrives.

prompt: With `--log-opt max-size=1m --log-opt max-file=3`, how many log files did the container's directory hold?
Ana adds `log-driver` and `log-opts` to `daemon.json` and restarts the daemon. Which containers rotate their logs?
hint: When are a container's log options decided?

choices.text: All of them, from the restart on
choices.why: Existing containers keep the options they were created with.
Right; the others keep theirs until they are recreated.

choices.text: None, until each image is rebuilt
choices.why: Logging is not part of an image.
The point of the daemon default is not to need the flag.

prompt: Why does a containerised program log to standard output rather than to `/var/log/shelf.log`?
hint: Who decides where the lines go?

choices.text: Writing files is forbidden in containers
choices.why: Containers write files all the time; it is a choice.

choices.text: Standard output is faster than a file
choices.why: Speed is not the argument.

choices.text: So the platform decides where lines go
choices.why: Right: the driver or an agent ships them, and the image does not change.
Some do, and it would not be the reason anyway.

choices.why: Speed is not why.

choices.text: The image has no `curl` and no shell to run it
choices.why: Right, on purpose since lesson 14; a tiny static binary fits.

hint: Which port did `shelf` listen on, and which did the check ask?

prompt: A standalone container turns `unhealthy`. What does the Docker daemon do about it?

choices.text: Restarts it, if it has a restart policy
choices.why: Restart policies react to the process exiting, not to health.

choices.text: Nothing; it only records the state
choices.why: Right: Compose, Swarm or a person has to act on it.
It keeps running.

choices.text: Replaces it with a new container from the same image
choices.why: That is what Swarm does, not the daemon on its own.

prompt: `shelf` moves to Kubernetes. What happens to its `HEALTHCHECK`?

choices.why: Kubernetes ignores the instruction.
The instruction is metadata; nothing refuses it.

choices.text: It is ignored; probes call `/health` instead
choices.why: Right, so the endpoint carries over even though the instruction does not.

choices.text: It becomes a liveness probe automatically
choices.why: Nothing converts it; probes are written in the manifest.

prompt: The `.netrc` was removed in the same `RUN` that wrote it. Why could `docker history` still show the token?
